09:00 Local Time, 07:00 GMT, 12:30 IST: Day 2 was all about Matt Renshaw and his career-best innings of 190. Having made his first Test hundred since 2017, the left-hander marshalled the lower order superbly and was involved in excellent stands for the 7th wicket and the 9th wicket with Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon respectively, hauling the Australians from 124 for 6 to a monumental score of 390. Renshaw's knock wasn't just gritty - he showed the typical left-hander elegance to blunt the hosts' bowling. He was the last man to be dismissed, but not before he had taken his team to a position of ascendency. It was immediately followed by the wicket of Ryan Rickelton, but Aiden Markram and David Bedingham ensured some stability. We are into Day 3 of the Test - it's typically a moving day and the Sunday crowd at the Kingsmead will hope for a strong riposte from the home team

'​You want to bat here, it looks like a superb batting surface. There are no real scarring or bruising marks, the wind is coming from the right direction and the sun is blazing. There's a bit of scarring, at around 4-5m, that's the end from where Keshav Maharaj bowled and that's the only area where the batters need to be careful about,' reckon Mark Nicholas and Shaun Pollock, in their pitch report

Matt Renshaw: (On his hundred) It's special; it's been a long time coming. I've been in this situation after a couple of opportunities. Just pleased to help the team out in a important Test match. I had an opportunity in 2023, but I didn't take it on some tough tours. Wasn't sure that I would play for Australia once again. Pretty special, I do think about my life and career. It's one of those, having opened the batting so much, you're used to leaving the ball. In the situation we had, we needed to survive. I needed to look at specifics. (On his batting against spin) The options I saw - there were two world-class spinners, so I wanted to disrupt them as much as I could by using many reverse sweeps, especially where I was trying to score, particularly with Nathan (Lyon) at the other end. I had to think about how many balls I needed to play, stay out in the middle and when to get to the other end.

15:55 Local Time, 13:55 GMT, 19:25 IST: South Africa added 46 runs in the session before being bowled out, and they'll look at that scorecard and wonder what might have been. Nine of their batters got into double digits, seven crossed 25, but none could push on to a substantial score, with Bedingham's 49 remaining the highest. The lack of big scores meant the absence of big partnerships too, though Maharaj and Harmer did stitch together a handy 52-run stand for the ninth wicket. Just when they seemed to be building something meaningful, Maharaj chipped one straight to mid-off. The last-wicket pair of Harmer and Nortje added a few more valuable runs, but Australia still walk away with a healthy lead of 106. The light has started to deteriorate, so it's unclear how much more play we'll get today. We'll be back shortly with Australia's second innings..
